sentences.zh: 天祐十八年，莊宗營於河上，議討鎮州。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Tianyou, Zhuangzong encamped on the Yellow River and deliberated attacking Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Tianyou, Zhuangzong encamped along the Yellow River and discussed a campaign against Zhen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 留守符存審在德勝寨未行，梁人謂莊宗已北，乃悉眾攻德勝，莊宗命明宗、存審為兩翼以抗之，自以中軍前進。

translations.literal: The garrison commander Fu Cunshen was at Desheng Stockade and had not yet marched. The Liang army thought Zhuangzong had gone north, so they massed all their forces to attack Desheng. Zhuangzong ordered Mingzong and Cunshen to form the two wings to resist them, while he himself advanced with the central army.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commander Fu Cunshen was still at Desheng Stockade and had not yet set out. The Liang forces, believing Zhuangzong had marched north, threw their whole strength against Desheng. Zhuangzong ordered Mingzong and Cunshen to take the two wings and meet the attack, while he led the center forward himself.

sentences.zh: 梁軍退卻，帝以十數騎雜梁軍而退，至壘門大呼，斬首數級，斧其望櫓而還。

translations.literal: When the Liang army withdrew, the Emperor rode with a dozen or so horsemen mixed among the Liang troops as they fell back. Reaching the barbican gate he shouted loudly, cut off several heads, hacked at their watchtower, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: As the Liang army pulled back, the Emperor rode with a dozen-odd horsemen concealed among the retreating enemy. At the barbican gate he shouted, cut down several men, chopped at their watchtower, and rode back.

sentences.zh: 莊宗大噱曰：「壯哉，阿三！

translations.literal: Zhuangzong laughed loudly and said, "How stalwart, A San!
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong laughed aloud and cried, "Splendid work, A San!

sentences.zh: 」賜酒一器。

translations.literal: " He bestowed one vessel of wine.
translations.idiomatic: " He rewarded him with a full cup of wine.

sentences.zh: 同光元年四月，從明宗襲破鄆州。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Tongguang, he followed Mingzong in a surprise attack that broke Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Tongguang, he accompanied Mingzong in a surprise assault that captured Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 九月，莊宗敗梁將王彥章於中都，急趨汴州。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Zhuangzong defeated the Liang general Wang Yanzhang at Zhongdu and hastened toward Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Zhuangzong defeated the Liang general Wang Yanzhang at Zhongdu and pressed hard toward Bian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明宗將前軍，帝率勁騎以從，晝夜兼行，率先下汴城。

translations.literal: Mingzong led the vanguard; the Emperor commanded crack cavalry to follow, traveling day and night without rest, and was first to descend into Bian city.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong commanded the van; the Emperor led elite cavalry in his train, marching day and night, and was the first to enter Bian city.

sentences.zh: 莊宗勞明宗曰：「復唐社稷，卿父子之功也。」

translations.literal: Zhuangzong commended Mingzong, saying, "Restoring the altars of Tang is the achievement of you father and son."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong praised Mingzong, saying, "To restore the house of Tang is the achievement of you and your son."

sentences.zh: 二年，以帝為衛州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year, the Emperor was appointed prefect of Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made prefect of Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時有王安節者，昭宗朝相杜讓能之宅吏也。

translations.literal: At that time there was one Wang Anjie, a household steward in the mansion of Chancellor Du Rangneng of Emperor Zhaozong's court.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was a man named Wang Anjie, formerly a household steward in the residence of Du Rangneng, a chancellor under Emperor Zhaozong.

sentences.zh: 安節少善賈，得相術於奇士，因事見帝於私邸，退謂人曰：「真北方天王相也，位當為天子，終則我莫知也。」

translations.literal: Anjie had been skilled in trade from youth and had learned physiognomy from a remarkable man. Because of this he came to see the Emperor at his private residence. On leaving he told others, "That is truly the physiognomy of the Heavenly King of the North; his position should be emperor, but as for how it ends, I do not know."
translations.idiomatic: Anjie had been adept at commerce since youth and had learned physiognomy from an extraordinary man. On business he called on the Emperor at his private residence. When he left he said to others, "That is truly the countenance of the Northern Heavenly King; he is destined for the throne, but how it will end I cannot tell."

sentences.zh: 三年，明宗奉詔北禦契丹，以家在太原，表帝為北京內衙指揮使；

translations.literal: In the third year, Mingzong received orders to march north against the Khitan. Because his family was in Taiyuan, he memorialized that the Emperor be made commander of the Northern Capital inner barracks;
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Mingzong was ordered north to resist the Khitan. As his household was in Taiyuan, he petitioned that the Emperor be appointed commander of the inner palace guard at the Northern Capital;

sentences.zh: 莊宗不悅，以帝為突騎都指揮使，遣戍石門。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong was displeased and made the Emperor commander of the Swift Cavalry, sending him to garrison Shimen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong was displeased and instead appointed him commander of the Swift Cavalry, posting him to garrison Shimen.

sentences.zh: 四年，魏州軍亂，明宗赴洛，時帝在橫水，率部下軍士由曲陽、孟縣趨常山，與王建立會，倍道兼行，渡河而南，由是明宗軍聲大振。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Wei Prefecture army mutinied and Mingzong went to Luoyang. At that time the Emperor was at Hengshui. He led his troops from Quyang and Meng County toward Changshan, joined Wang Jianli, traveled by forced marches day and night, crossed the river and marched south, and thereby Mingzong's army's renown greatly rose.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the troops at Wei Prefecture mutinied and Mingzong set out for Luoyang. The Emperor was then at Hengshui. He led his men by way of Quyang and Meng County to Changshan, where he joined Wang Jianli. They pressed south by forced marches, crossed the river, and from that time Mingzong's army gained tremendous momentum.

sentences.zh: 天成初，以帝為河中節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng, the Emperor was made military commissioner of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tiancheng era he was appointed military commissioner of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，加檢校太保、同平章事。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year, he was given the additional titles of Grand Guardian and Co-Manager of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year he was further named Grand Guardian and appointed co-manager of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 十一月，加檢校太傅。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, he was given the additional title of Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was further named Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 長興元年，加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changxing, he was given the additional title of Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Changxing he was further named Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝興樞密使安重誨在常山，因杯盤失意，帝以拳擊重誨腦，中其櫛，走而獲免。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Emperor and the Commissioner of Military Affairs An Chonghui were at Changshan. Over a lapse at the wine table, the Emperor struck Chonghui on the head with his fist, hitting his comb; Chonghui fled and escaped injury.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while the Emperor and the commissioner of military affairs An Chonghui were at Changshan, a quarrel over the wine cups angered the Emperor, who struck Chonghui on the head with his fist and knocked his comb askew. Chonghui ran off and escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 帝雖悔謝，然重誨終銜之。

translations.literal: Although the Emperor regretted it and apologized, Chonghui nevertheless bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Emperor repented and apologized, Chonghui never forgave the affront.

sentences.zh: 及帝鎮河中，重誨知其出入不時，因矯宣中旨，令牙將楊彥溫遇出郭則閉門勿納。

translations.literal: When the Emperor governed Hezhong, Chonghui knew that he came and went at irregular hours. He therefore forged an imperial order instructing the garrison officer Yang Yanwen that whenever the Prince went outside the city walls, the gates were to be shut and he was not to be admitted.
translations.idiomatic: After the Emperor took command at Hezhong, Chonghui, knowing that he came and went at odd hours, forged an order in the emperor's name telling the garrison officer Yang Yanwen to shut the gates whenever the prince left the city and refuse him entry on his return.

sentences.zh: 是歲四月五日，帝閱馬於黃龍莊，彥溫閉城拒帝，帝聞難遽還，遣問其故，彥溫曰：「但請相公入朝，此城不可入也。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the fourth month that year, the Emperor was reviewing horses at Huanglong Manor. Yanwen shut the city and barred the Emperor. Hearing of the trouble he hurried back and sent someone to ask the reason. Yanwen said, "I only ask that the Lord Chancellor enter court; this city may not be entered."
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the fourth month that year the Emperor was inspecting horses at Huanglong Manor. Yanwen closed the city and barred him. Hearing of the trouble, the Emperor rode back at once and sent to ask why. Yanwen replied, "I beg the lord only to proceed to court; this city cannot be entered."

sentences.zh: 」帝止虞鄉以聞，明宗詔帝歸闕。

translations.literal: " The Emperor halted at Yuxiang and reported the matter. Mingzong ordered the Emperor to return to court.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor stopped at Yuxiang and reported what had happened. Mingzong ordered him to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 遣藥彥稠將兵討彥溫，令生致之，麵要鞫問。

translations.literal: He sent Yao Yanchou to lead troops against Yanwen, ordering that he be taken alive and brought bound for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Yao Yanchou with an army to punish Yanwen, with orders to take him alive and bring him in bonds for questioning.

sentences.zh: 十一月收城，彥溫已死，明宗以彥稠不能生致彥溫，甚怒之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the city was taken, but Yanwen was already dead. Mingzong was very angry that Yanchou had failed to take Yanwen alive.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the city was recovered, but Yanwen was already dead. Mingzong was furious that Yanchou had not captured him alive.

sentences.zh: 後數日，安重誨以帝失守，諷宰相論奏行法，明宗不悅。

translations.literal: Several days later, An Chonghui, on the grounds that the Emperor had lost his post, prompted the chief ministers to memorialize that the law be applied. Mingzong was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later An Chonghui, citing the prince's loss of his command, urged the chief ministers to memorialize for legal punishment. Mingzong was displeased.

sentences.zh: 重誨又自論奏，明宗曰：「 朕為小將校時，家徒衣食不足，賴此兒荷石灰、收馬糞存養，以至今貴為天子，而不能庇一兒！

translations.literal: Chonghui again memorialized on his own. Mingzong said, " When I was a junior officer my household had nothing but insufficient food and clothing. I relied on this boy carrying lime and gathering horse dung to support me, until today I have risen to be honored as Son of Heaven, yet I cannot protect one son!
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui submitted another memorial on his own. Mingzong said, "When I was a junior officer my family scarcely had food or clothing. I depended on this boy, who carried lime and gathered horse dung to keep us alive, until I rose to be emperor—and now I cannot shelter one son!

sentences.zh: 卿欲行朝典，朕未曉其意，卿等可速退，從他私第閑坐。

translations.literal: You wish to apply the statutes of court; I do not understand your intent. You may all withdraw at once and go sit idly in your private residences."
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to invoke the law of the court, I do not understand your meaning. Withdraw at once and go idle in your private mansions."

sentences.zh: 」遂詔歸清化裏第，不預朝請。

translations.literal: " He then ordered the Emperor to return to his residence in Qinghua Lane and not to attend court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered the prince back to his residence in Qinghua Lane, barred from court attendance.

sentences.zh: 帝尚懼重誨多方危陷，但日諷佛書陰禱而已。

translations.literal: The Emperor still feared that Chonghui would in many ways endanger and entrap him, and could only daily chant Buddhist scriptures and pray in secret.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor still feared that Chonghui would find other ways to destroy him and could only recite Buddhist texts and pray in secret each day.

sentences.zh: 二年，安重誨得罪，帝即授左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year, An Chonghui fell from favor, and the Emperor was at once appointed general of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, after An Chonghui fell from power, the Emperor was immediately appointed general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復檢校太傅、同平章事、行京兆尹，充西京留守。

translations.literal: Before long he was again given the titles of Grand Tutor and Co-Manager of Affairs, acted as metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, and served as garrison commander of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was again named Grand Tutor and co-manager of state affairs, acted as metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, and was made garrison commander of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 三年，進位太尉，移鳳翔節度使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to Grand Commandant and transferred to military commissioner of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to Grand Commandant and transferred to the Fengxiang command.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，封潞王。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year he was enfeoffed as Prince of Lu.

sentences.zh: 閔帝即位，加兼侍中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min ascended the throne, the Emperor was additionally made chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min came to the throne, the prince was additionally appointed chief minister.

sentences.zh: 既而帝子重吉出刺亳州，女尼入宮，帝方憂不測。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the Emperor's son Chongji was sent out as prefect of Bo Prefecture, and a daughter who had become a nun entered the palace. The Emperor then began to fear what might befall him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his son Chongji was posted as prefect of Bo Prefecture, and a daughter who had taken vows as a nun was summoned into the palace. The prince began to fear for his life.

sentences.zh: 應順元年二月，移帝鎮太原，是時不降制書，唯以宣授而已。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Yingshun, the Emperor was transferred to command Taiyuan. At that time no formal edict was issued; there was only an oral appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Yingshun he was ordered to take command at Taiyuan. No formal edict was issued—only an announcement by imperial messenger.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，召賓佐將吏以謀之，皆曰：「主上年幼，未親庶事，軍國大政悉委朱宏昭等，王必無保全之理。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard this, he summoned his staff, aides, and officers to deliberate. All said, "The sovereign is young and has not yet personally attended to ordinary affairs. All great matters of army and state are entrusted to Zhu Hongzhao and the like. Your Highness will certainly have no way to preserve yourself."
translations.idiomatic: When he heard the news, he called his staff and commanders to counsel together. All said, "The emperor is young and does not yet handle daily affairs himself. Military and civil power rests entirely with Zhu Hongzhao and his faction. Your Highness cannot hope to survive."

sentences.zh: 」判官馬裔孫曰：「君命召，不俟駕行焉。

translations.literal: " The aide Ma Yisun said, "When the ruler's command summons, one does not wait for the carriage to set out."
translations.idiomatic: " The aide Ma Yisun said, "When the sovereign summons, one does not wait even to harness the carriage."

sentences.zh: 諸君凶言，非令圖也。

translations.literal: Your ominous words, gentlemen, are no proper plan."
translations.idiomatic: Such grim talk, gentlemen, is no sound plan."

sentences.zh: 」是夜，帝令李專美草檄求援諸道，欲誅君側之罪。

translations.literal: " That night the Emperor ordered Li Zhuanmei to draft a proclamation seeking aid from the various circuits, intending to punish the crimes of those at the ruler's side.
translations.idiomatic: " That night he ordered Li Zhuanmei to draft a proclamation calling on the circuits for aid, declaring his intent to punish the evil counselors at court.

sentences.zh: 朝廷命王思同率師來討。

translations.literal: The court ordered Wang Sitong to lead an army against him.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Wang Sitong to lead troops against him.

sentences.zh: 三月十五日，外兵大集。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day of the third month, the outside armies massed in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth day of the third month the besieging armies gathered in force.

sentences.zh: 《九國誌·李彥琦傳》：潞王守岐下，諸道將急攻其壘，彥琦時在圍中，罄家財以給軍用。）

translations.literal: (From the Biography of Li Yanqi in the Jiuguozhi: When the Prince of Lu held the lower reaches of Qi, the generals of the various circuits urgently attacked his camp. Yanqi was then within the siege and exhausted his family wealth to supply military expenses.)
translations.idiomatic: (From the Biography of Li Yanqi in the Jiuguozhi: While the Prince of Lu held the lower Qi region, generals from the various circuits pressed the attack on his camp. Yanqi was then inside the siege and spent his entire family fortune to supply the army.)

sentences.zh: 十六日，大將督眾攻外城，帝登城垂泣，諭於外曰：「我年未二十從先帝征伐，出生入死，金瘡滿身，樹立得社稷，軍士從我登陣者多矣。

translations.literal: On the sixteenth day the great generals directed the masses to attack the outer city. The Emperor ascended the wall and wept as he addressed those outside, saying, "Before I was twenty I followed the late emperor in campaigns, facing death at every turn until my body was covered with wounds of gold. I helped establish the altars of state. Many soldiers who followed me into battle have fallen."
translations.idiomatic: On the sixteenth the chief generals pressed the assault on the outer wall. The prince mounted the ramparts in tears and called out to the besiegers: "Before I was twenty I followed the late emperor to war, risking my life again and again until my body was scarred with old wounds. I helped raise the dynasty. How many soldiers who marched with me have died on the field!"

sentences.zh: 今朝廷信任賊臣，殘害骨肉，且我有何罪！

translations.literal: Now the court trusts treacherous ministers and harms its own flesh and blood—and what crime have I committed!
translations.idiomatic: Now the court trusts traitors and destroys its own kin—what crime have I committed?

sentences.zh: 」因慟哭，聞者哀之。

translations.literal: " He then sobbed in anguish, and those who heard were moved to grief.
translations.idiomatic: " He broke into loud weeping, and all who heard were stricken with sorrow.

sentences.zh: 時羽林都指揮使楊思權謂眾曰：「大相公，吾主也。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Siquan, commander of the Imperial Guard, said to the troops, "The Great Lord is my sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: Then Yang Siquan, commander of the Imperial Guard, cried to the men, "The Great Lord is my master."

sentences.zh: 」遂引軍自西門入，嚴衛都指揮使尹暉亦引軍自東門而入，外軍悉潰。

translations.literal: " He then led his army in through the west gate. Yin Hui, commander of the Palace Guard, also led his troops in through the east gate, and the outside armies all collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: " He led his men in through the west gate. Yin Hui, commander of the Palace Guard, brought his troops in through the east gate as well, and the besieging armies broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 十七日，率居民家財以賞軍士。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth day he took the households' wealth of the residents to reward the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth he seized civilian wealth from the townspeople to reward his troops.

sentences.zh: 是日，帝整眾而東。

translations.literal: That day the Emperor marshaled his forces and marched east.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he marshaled his army and marched east.

sentences.zh: 二十日，次長安，副留守劉遂雍以城降，率京兆居民家財犒軍。

translations.literal: On the twentieth day he halted at Chang'an. The deputy garrison commander Liu Suiyong surrendered the city and led the residents of Jingzhao to offer their household wealth to feast the army.
translations.idiomatic: On the twentieth he reached Chang'an. The deputy garrison commander Liu Suiyong surrendered the city and levied the wealth of Jingzhao households to reward the army.

sentences.zh: 二十三日，次靈口，誅王思同。

translations.literal: On the twenty-third day he halted at Lingkou and executed Wang Sitong.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-third he halted at Lingkou and executed Wang Sitong.

sentences.zh: 二十四日，次華州，收藥彥稠係獄。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fourth day he halted at Hua Prefecture and had Yao Yanchou seized and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fourth he halted at Hua Prefecture and had Yao Yanchou arrested and thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 二十五日，次閿鄉，王仲皋父子迎謁，命誅之。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fifth day he halted at Wenxiang. Wang Zhonggao father and son came out to greet him, and he ordered them executed.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fifth he halted at Wenxiang. Wang Zhonggao and his son came out to pay their respects, and he ordered them put to death.

sentences.zh: 二十六日，次靈寶，河中節度使安彥威來降，待罪，宥之，遣歸鎮。

translations.literal: On the twenty-sixth day he halted at Lingbao. An Yanwei, military commissioner of Hezhong, came to surrender, awaiting punishment. The Emperor pardoned him and sent him back to his post.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-sixth he halted at Lingbao. An Yanwei, military commissioner of Hezhong, came to submit and await judgment. The prince pardoned him and sent him back to his command.

sentences.zh: 陝州節度使康思立奉迎。

translations.literal: Kang Sili, military commissioner of Shan Prefecture, came out to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Sili, military commissioner of Shan Prefecture, came out to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 二十七日，次陝州，下令告諭京城。

translations.literal: On the twenty-seventh day he halted at Shan Prefecture and issued an order proclaiming his message to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-seventh he halted at Shan Prefecture and issued a proclamation to the capital.

sentences.zh: 二十八日，康義誠軍前兵士相繼來降，義誠詣軍門請罪，帝宥之。

translations.literal: On the twenty-eighth day the soldiers before Kang Yicheng's army came over in succession to surrender. Yicheng came to the army gate to plead guilty, and the Emperor pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-eighth the soldiers in Kang Yicheng's van surrendered one after another. Yicheng came to the camp gate to plead for mercy, and the prince pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 駕下諸軍畢至，誅宣徽南院使孟漢瓊於路左。

translations.literal: All the armies under the imperial carriage had now arrived, and Meng Hanqiong, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was executed on the left of the road.
translations.idiomatic: When all the armies of the court had gathered, Meng Hanqiong, commissioner of the southern bureau of the palace secretariat, was executed by the roadside.

sentences.zh: 是夜，閔帝與帳下親騎百餘出元武門而去。

translations.literal: That night Emperor Min, with a little more than a hundred personal cavalry from his entourage, went out through the Xuanwu Gate and fled.
translations.idiomatic: That night Emperor Min fled through the Xuanwu Gate with a little more than a hundred of his personal cavalry.

sentences.zh: 夏四月壬申，帝至蔣橋，文武百官立班奉迎，教旨以未拜梓宮，未可相見，俟會於至德宮，時六軍勳臣及節將內職已累表勸進。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on the day renshen, the Emperor reached Jiang Bridge. The civil and military officials formed ranks to welcome him. An edict stated that because he had not yet paid respects before the coffin, they could not yet meet face to face, and they should wait to assemble at Zhide Palace. At that time the meritorious officers of the Six Armies, the military commissioners, and the inner-service officials had repeatedly memorialized urging his advance to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on renshen, the prince reached Jiang Bridge. Civil and military officials formed ranks to welcome him. An edict explained that, as he had not yet bowed before the coffin, they could not meet yet and should await him at Zhide Palace. By then the meritorious officers of the Six Armies, the military commissioners, and the inner-court officials had already submitted repeated memorials urging him to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 是日，帝入謁太后、太妃，至西宮，伏梓宮慟哭，宰相與百僚班見致拜，帝答拜。

translations.literal: That day the Emperor entered to pay respects to the Empress Dowager and the Senior Consort. He went to the Western Palace, prostrated himself before the coffin, and wept in anguish. The chief ministers and the hundred officials formed ranks, came forward, and bowed; the Emperor returned their bows.
translations.idiomatic: That day he entered to pay his respects to the empress dowager and the senior consort, then went to the Western Palace, where he prostrated himself before the coffin and wept bitterly. The chief ministers and the full bureaucracy came forward in ranks to bow; he returned their bows.

sentences.zh: 馮道等上箋勸進，帝立謂群臣曰：「予之此行，事非獲已，當俟主上歸闕，園陵禮終，退守藩服。

translations.literal: Feng Dao and others submitted a memorial urging his advance. The Emperor stood and said to the assembled ministers, "My expedition on this occasion was not something I could avoid. I should wait until the sovereign returns to court and the rites at the imperial tombs are completed, then withdraw to guard my fief."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao and others submitted a memorial urging him to ascend the throne. Standing before the assembly, he said, "This campaign was not undertaken willingly. I mean to wait until the emperor returns to court and the tomb rites are finished, then withdraw to my fief."

sentences.zh: 諸公言遽及此，信無謂也。

translations.literal: For you gentlemen to speak so hastily of this is truly meaningless."
translations.idiomatic: For you to press this matter so soon is truly absurd."

sentences.zh: 」衛州刺史王宏贄奏，閔帝以前月二十九日至州。

translations.literal: " Wang Hongzan, prefect of Wei Prefecture, memorialized that Emperor Min had reached the prefecture on the twenty-ninth day of the previous month.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Hongzan, prefect of Wei Prefecture, reported that Emperor Min had arrived in his jurisdiction on the twenty-ninth of the previous month.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，皇太后下令降閔帝為鄂王。

translations.literal: On the day guiyou, the Empress Dowager issued an order demoting Emperor Min to Prince of E.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou the empress dowager ordered Emperor Min demoted to Prince of E.

sentences.zh: 又，太后令曰：「 先皇帝誕膺天眷，光紹帝圖，明誠動於三靈，德澤被於四海，方期偃革，遽歎遺弓。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Empress Dowager's order said, " The late emperor received Heaven's favor at his birth, brilliantly continuing the imperial design. His bright sincerity moved the Three Spirits, and his virtue and grace spread through the Four Seas. Just as we looked forward to laying down arms, we suddenly lamented the loss of the bow."
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager also issued an order: "The late emperor was born under Heaven's favor and brilliantly carried on the imperial enterprise. His sincerity moved heaven, earth, and the spirits; his virtue reached the four seas. Just as we hoped to lay down arms, we were suddenly bereft of our ruler."

sentences.zh: 自少主之承祧，為奸臣之擅命，離間骨肉，猜忌磐維，既輒易於藩垣，復驟興於兵甲。

translations.literal: Since the young sovereign inherited the ancestral line, treacherous ministers have usurped authority, estranging flesh and blood, breeding suspicion among the firm roots of the state. They have repeatedly shifted the feudal barriers and again suddenly raised arms.
translations.idiomatic: Since the young emperor succeeded to the line, traitorous ministers have seized power, driving kin apart and sowing suspicion among the pillars of the realm. They have repeatedly shifted princes among their fiefs and again suddenly raised armies.

sentences.zh: 遂致輕離社稷，大撓軍民，萬世鴻基，將墜於地。

translations.literal: This has caused the altars of state to be lightly abandoned, greatly shaken army and people, and the great foundation of ten thousand generations is about to fall to earth.
translations.idiomatic: They have nearly torn the dynasty from its foundations, thrown army and people into turmoil, and brought the eternal enterprise to the brink of ruin.

sentences.zh: 皇長子潞王從珂，位居塚嗣，德茂衝年，乃武乃文，惟忠惟孝。

translations.literal: The eldest imperial son, the Prince of Lu Congke, stands in the position of heir to the ancestral shrine. His virtue flourished from youth. He is martial and literary, loyal and filial.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest imperial son, the Prince of Lu Congke, stands as heir to the ancestral shrine. His virtue has been abundant since youth. He is both warrior and scholar, loyal and filial in equal measure.

sentences.zh: 前朝廓清多難，有戰伐之大功；

translations.literal: In the previous reign he cleared away many hardships and has great achievements in battle and campaign;
translations.idiomatic: In the previous reign he cleared away countless dangers and won great distinction in war;

sentences.zh: 纘紹丕圖，有夾輔之盛業。

translations.literal: he has continued the great design and has magnificent achievements as supporter at the ruler's side.
translations.idiomatic: he has upheld the great enterprise and rendered magnificent service as a pillar of the throne.

sentences.zh: 今以宗祧乏祀，園寢有期，須委親賢，俾居監撫，免萬機之壅滯，慰兆庶之推崇。

translations.literal: Now because the ancestral line lacks sacrifice and the imperial tombs have their appointed season, we must entrust a close and worthy man to reside in regency, to free the myriad affairs from obstruction and to comfort the myriad people in their high regard.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the ancestral line lacks proper rites and the tomb observances draw near, we must entrust a close and worthy kinsman with regency, to keep the myriad affairs of state from stalling and to satisfy the people's eager hopes.

sentences.zh: 可起今月四日知軍國事，權以書詔印施行。

translations.literal: He may from the fourth day of this month take charge of military and civil affairs, provisionally using the imperial seal on documents and edicts to put orders into effect.
translations.idiomatic: Let him assume charge of military and civil affairs from the fourth day of this month, acting provisionally under the imperial seal on written orders.

sentences.zh: 」是日，監國在至德宮，宰臣馮道等率百官班於宮門待罪。

translations.literal: " That day the regent was at Zhide Palace. The chief minister Feng Dao and others led the hundred officials in ranks at the palace gate to await judgment on their guilt.
translations.idiomatic: " That day the regent was at Zhide Palace. Chief minister Feng Dao and the rest led the bureaucracy in ranks at the palace gate to await judgment.

sentences.zh: 帝出於庭，曰：「相公諸人何罪，請復位。

translations.literal: The Emperor came out into the courtyard and said, "What crime have you chief ministers committed? Please resume your places."
translations.idiomatic: The prince came out into the courtyard and said, "What offense have you chief ministers committed? Please return to your posts."

sentences.zh: 」乃退。

translations.literal: " He then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " He then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，太后令曰：「先皇帝櫛風沐雨，平定華夷，嗣洪業於艱難，致蒼生於富庶。

translations.literal: On the day jiaxu, the Empress Dowager's order said, "The late emperor braved wind and rain, pacified China and the barbarians, inherited the great enterprise amid hardship, and brought the black-haired people to wealth and plenty."
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu the empress dowager issued an order: "The late emperor endured wind and rain, pacified the realm, inherited the great enterprise through hardship, and brought the people to prosperity."

sentences.zh: 鄂王嗣位，奸臣弄權，作福作威，不誠不信，離間骨肉，猜忌磐維。

translations.literal: The Prince of E succeeded to the throne; treacherous ministers manipulated power, bestowing favor and wielding authority, without sincerity or trustworthiness, estranging flesh and blood and breeding suspicion among the firm roots of the state.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of E succeeded to the throne, evil ministers seized power, dispensing favors and terror alike, false and faithless, driving kin apart and sowing suspicion among the pillars of the realm.

sentences.zh: 鄂王輕舍宗祧，不克負荷，洪基大寶，危若綴旒，須立長君，以紹丕構。

translations.literal: The Prince of E lightly abandoned the ancestral line and could not bear the burden. The great foundation and imperial treasure hung as precariously as a pendant gem on a thread. A senior ruler must be established to continue the great structure.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of E lightly cast aside the ancestral line and proved unable to bear the burden. The throne hung as precariously as a gem on a thread. A mature ruler must be enthroned to carry on the great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 皇長子潞王從珂，日躋孝敬，天縱聰明，有神武之英姿，有寬仁之偉略。

translations.literal: The eldest imperial son, the Prince of Lu Congke, daily advances in filial respect. Heaven has endowed him with intelligence. He has a divine and martial heroic bearing and a broad and benevolent grand strategy.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest imperial son, the Prince of Lu Congke, grows daily in filial devotion. Heaven has gifted him with keen intelligence, a heroic martial bearing, and a broad and benevolent vision.

sentences.zh: 先朝經綸草昧，廓靜寰區，辛勤有百戰之勞，忠貞讚一統之運，臣誠子道，冠古超今。

translations.literal: In the previous court he governed amid the chaos of founding, cleared and pacified the realm, toiled through the labor of a hundred battles, and with loyal steadfastness praised the fortune of unified rule. As minister he was sincere; as son he was filial—surpassing antiquity and exceeding the present age.
translations.idiomatic: In the previous reign he helped govern from the chaos of founding, pacified the realm, endured the toil of a hundred battles, and with loyal steadfastness upheld the fortune of reunification. In service as minister and in conduct as son he has surpassed all ages.

sentences.zh: 而又克己化民，推心撫士，率土之謳歌有屬，上蒼之眷命攸臨。

translations.literal: Moreover he restrains himself and transforms the people, opens his heart and comforts the officers. Throughout the realm songs of praise have their object, and the blue heaven's favoring mandate draws near.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he disciplines himself and transforms the people, treats his officers with open sincerity, and has won the songs of the realm. Heaven's favoring mandate is upon him.

sentences.zh: 一日萬機，不可以暫曠；

translations.literal: The myriad affairs of a single day cannot be left vacant even briefly;
translations.idiomatic: The myriad affairs of state cannot be left unattended even for a day;

sentences.zh: 九州四海，不可以無歸。

translations.literal: the Nine Provinces and Four Seas cannot be without a destination.
translations.idiomatic: the nine provinces and four seas cannot be left without a sovereign.

sentences.zh: 況因山有期，同軌斯至，永言嗣守，屬任元良，宜即皇帝位。」

translations.literal: Moreover, as the mountain rites have their appointed time and the unified tracks will soon arrive, to continue and guard forever we entrust the heir apparent. He should immediately ascend the imperial throne."
translations.idiomatic: Now that the tomb rites draw near and the realm will soon be reunited under one rule, the succession must be secured and the heir entrusted with the charge. Let him immediately ascend the imperial throne."

sentences.zh: 乙亥，監國赴西宮，柩前告奠即位。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, the regent went to the Western Palace and, before the bier, announced the offering and ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the regent went to the Western Palace and, before the coffin, performed the offering rites and took the throne.

sentences.zh: 攝中書令李愚宣冊書曰：

translations.literal: Li Yu, acting as Director of the Secretariat, proclaimed the investiture document, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu, acting director of the secretariat, read the investiture document:

sentences.zh: 維應順元年歲次甲午，四月庚午朔，六日乙亥，文武百僚，特進、守司空兼門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事、充太微宮使、弘文館大學士、上柱國、始平郡公、食邑二千五百戶臣馮道等九千五百九十三人上言：帝王興運，天地同符，河出圖而洛出書，雲從龍而風從虎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yingshun, year jiawu, on the first day of the fourth month, gengwu, the sixth day yihai, the civil and military hundred officials—Special Advancement, Acting Minister of Works and Vice Director of the Chancellery, Co-Director of the Secretariat and Chancellery, Commissioner of the Taiwei Palace, Grand Academician of the Hongwen Institute, Upper Pillar of State, Duke of Shiping with a fief of two thousand five hundred households, your subject Feng Dao, together with nine thousand five hundred ninety-three persons—memorialized: When an emperor's fortune rises, heaven and earth share the same sign. The Yellow River produces the chart and the Luo River produces the writing; clouds follow the dragon and wind follows the tiger.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yingshun, the jiawu year, on gengwu, the first day of the fourth month, yihai, the sixth day, the civil and military officials—among them Feng Dao, Special Advancement, Acting Minister of Works and Vice Director of the Chancellery, Co-Director of the Secretariat and Chancellery, Commissioner of the Taiwei Palace, Grand Academician of the Hongwen Institute, Upper Pillar of State, Duke of Shiping with a fief of two thousand five hundred households, together with nine thousand five hundred ninety-three others—memorialized: When an emperor's fortune rises, heaven and earth bear the same sign. The Yellow River yields the chart and the Luo River the writing; clouds follow the dragon and wind the tiger.

sentences.zh: 莫不恢張八表，覆育兆民，立大定之基，保無疆之祚。

translations.literal: None fail to extend their sway over the eight directions, nurture and shelter the myriad people, establish the foundation of great stability, and preserve boundless fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Such rulers invariably extend their sway to the eight directions, nurture the myriad people, lay the foundation of lasting order, and secure boundless fortune.

sentences.zh: 人謠再洽，天命顯歸，須登宸極之尊，以奉祖宗之祀。

translations.literal: The people's songs again harmonize; Heaven's mandate clearly returns. One must ascend to the august pinnacle to serve the sacrifices to the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: The people's songs again unite in praise; Heaven's mandate clearly rests upon you. You must ascend the imperial throne to perform the ancestral rites.

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇帝陛下，天資仁智，神助機權，奉莊宗於多難之時，從先帝於四征之際，凡當決勝，無不成功。

translations.literal: We humbly consider that Your Majesty, endowed by Heaven with benevolence and wisdom and divinely aided in strategy and authority, served Zhuangzong in times of many hardships and followed the late emperor through four campaigns. Whenever decisive victory was needed, none was not achieved.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly consider that Your Majesty, endowed with Heaven's benevolence and wisdom and divinely aided in counsel and command, served Zhuangzong through many hardships and followed the late emperor through four campaigns. In every decisive moment, victory was yours.

sentences.zh: 洎正皇綱，每嚴師律，為國家之志大，守臣子之道全。

translations.literal: When the imperial order was set right, he always enforced military discipline strictly. His ambition for the state was great, and his observance of the way of subject and son was complete.
translations.idiomatic: Once the imperial order was restored, he enforced military discipline without fail. His ambition for the state was great, and his conduct as subject and son was beyond reproach.

sentences.zh: 自泣遺弓，常悲易月，欲期同軌，親赴因山。

translations.literal: Since weeping over the lost bow, he has constantly grieved at the change of month, wishing to await the unified tracks and personally attend the mountain rites.
translations.idiomatic: Since the late emperor's passing he has mourned deeply, longing for the day when the realm would be reunited and he could personally attend the tomb rites.

sentences.zh: 而自鄂王承祧，奸臣擅命，致神祇之乏饗，激朝野以歸心。

translations.literal: Yet since the Prince of E inherited the line, treacherous ministers have usurped authority, causing the spirits to lack offerings and stirring court and countryside to turn their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Yet since the Prince of E took the throne, traitorous ministers have usurped power, leaving the spirits without proper offerings and turning court and countryside alike toward you.

sentences.zh: 使屈者伸，令否者泰，人情大順，天象至明。

translations.literal: He has made the bent straight and turned denial into peace. Human sentiment is greatly aligned; the heavenly signs are supremely clear.
translations.idiomatic: You have set right what was wrong and turned adversity into peace. The people's hearts are united, and the heavens show their clearest signs.

sentences.zh: 聚東井以呈祥，拱北辰而應運。

translations.literal: Stars gather at the Eastern Well to display auspicious signs; they surround the Northern Pole and respond to the turning fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Stars gather at the Eastern Well in auspicious array; they circle the Northern Pole in answer to the mandate of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 由是文武百辟，嶽牧群賢，至於比屋之倫，盡祝當陽之位。

translations.literal: Therefore the civil and military hundred ministers, the governors and herdsmen among the assembled worthies, and even households door to door—all pray for the position facing the sun.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason the civil and military ministers, the governors and worthies of the realm, and even common households one and all pray that you take the throne.

sentences.zh: 今則承太后慈旨，守先朝遠圖，撫四海九州，享千齡萬祀。

translations.literal: Now then, in accordance with the Empress Dowager's merciful decree and guarding the late emperor's far-reaching design, he will soothe the four seas and nine provinces and enjoy a thousand ages and ten thousand sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Now, in obedience to the empress dowager's gracious command and faithful to the late emperor's far-reaching design, may he bring peace to the four seas and nine provinces and enjoy a thousand years of rule.

sentences.zh: 臣等不勝大願，謹上寶冊，稟太后令，奉皇帝踐祚。

translations.literal: Your subjects cannot contain their great wish. We reverently present the precious document, obeying the Empress Dowager's order, to install the Emperor on the throne.
translations.idiomatic: We, your subjects, cannot contain our deepest wish. We reverently present the imperial register, obeying the empress dowager's command, to install Your Majesty upon the throne.

sentences.zh: 臣等誠慶誠忭，謹言。

translations.literal: Your subjects are sincerely joyous and sincerely delighted; we respectfully state.
translations.idiomatic: We are sincerely overjoyed and respectfully submit this memorial.

sentences.zh: 帝就殿之東楹受群臣稱賀。

translations.literal: The Emperor received the congratulations of the assembled ministers at the eastern pillar of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received the congratulations of the assembled ministers at the eastern pillar of the hall.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝在鳳翔日，有瞽者張濛自言知術數，事太白山神，其神祠即元魏時崔浩廟也。

translations.literal: Earlier, while the Emperor was at Fengxiang, there was a blind man Zhang Meng who claimed to know numerology and served the spirit of Mount Taibai. That spirit shrine was the temple of Cui Hao from the Northern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while the prince was at Fengxiang, a blind man named Zhang Meng claimed skill in divination and served the spirit of Mount Taibai—the shrine being the temple of Cui Hao from the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 時之否泰，人之休咎，濛告於神，即傳吉凶之言，帝親校房暠酷信之。

translations.literal: Whether times were adverse or prosperous, and whether people's fortunes were good or ill, Meng reported to the spirit, who then transmitted words of fortune or calamity. The Emperor's personal attendant Fang Hao trusted him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Whether times were good or ill, whether men's fortunes rose or fell, Meng would consult the spirit and relay its words of fortune or disaster. The prince's personal attendant Fang Hao believed him completely.

sentences.zh: 一日，濛至府，聞帝語聲，駭然曰：「非人臣也。

translations.literal: One day Meng came to the mansion. Hearing the Emperor's voice, he cried out in alarm, "That is no mere subject."
translations.idiomatic: One day Meng came to the mansion. Hearing the prince speak, he cried out in alarm, "That is no ordinary subject."

sentences.zh: 」暠詢其事，即傳神語曰：「三珠並一珠，驢馬沒人驅，歲月甲庚午，中興戊己土。

translations.literal: " Hao asked what this meant, and he transmitted the spirit's words: "Three pearls merge into one pearl; donkeys and horses are driven by no man; the year is jiawu; restoration lies in wu and ji earth."
translations.idiomatic: " Hao asked what it meant, and Meng relayed the spirit's words: "Three pearls merge into one pearl; donkeys and horses have no driver; the year is jiawu; restoration lies in wu and ji earth."

sentences.zh: 」暠請解釋，曰：「神言予不知也。

translations.literal: " Hao asked for an explanation. He said, "The spirit's words—I do not understand them."
translations.idiomatic: " Hao asked for an explanation. Meng said, "I do not understand the spirit's words myself."

sentences.zh: 」長興四年五月，府廨諸門無故自動，人頗駭異。

translations.literal: " In the fifth month of the fourth year of Changxing, the various gates of the official compound opened by themselves for no reason, and people were much alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fifth month of the fourth year of Changxing, every gate of the official compound swung open by itself, to everyone's alarm.

sentences.zh: 遣暠問濛，濛曰：「衙署小異勿怪，不出三日，當有恩命。

translations.literal: He sent Hao to ask Meng. Meng said, "Minor oddities at the yamen need not alarm you. Within three days there will be an imperial grace."
translations.idiomatic: The prince sent Hao to ask Meng, who said, "Do not be alarmed by small oddities at the yamen. Within three days an imperial favor will arrive."

sentences.zh: 」是夜報至，封潞王。

translations.literal: " That night the report arrived: enfeoffment as Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: " That very night the order came: he was enfeoffed as Prince of Lu.

sentences.zh: 及帝移鎮河東，甚懼，問濛，濛曰：「王保無患。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was transferred to command Hedong, he was greatly afraid and asked Meng. Meng said, "Your Highness is assuredly without trouble."
translations.idiomatic: When the prince was transferred to command Hedong, he was terrified and asked Meng, who said, "Your Highness need have no fear."

sentences.zh: 」王思同兵至，又詰之，濛曰：「王有天下，不能獨力，朝廷兵來迎王也。

translations.literal: " When Wang Sitong's army arrived, he questioned him again. Meng said, "Your Highness will possess the realm but cannot do it alone. The court's army comes to welcome Your Highness."
translations.idiomatic: " When Wang Sitong's army arrived, he questioned Meng again, who said, "Your Highness will gain the realm but cannot do it alone. The court's army comes to welcome you."

sentences.zh: 王若疑臣，臣唯一子，請王致之麾下，以質臣心。

translations.literal: "If Your Highness doubts me, I have only one son. I ask that Your Highness take him into your camp as a pledge of my sincerity."
translations.idiomatic: "If Your Highness doubts me, I have only one son. I beg you to take him into your service as a pledge of my loyalty."

sentences.zh: 」帝乃以濛攝館驛巡官。

translations.literal: " The Emperor then made Meng acting patrol officer of the post station.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince then appointed Meng acting patrol officer of the courier stations.

sentences.zh: 至是，帝受冊，冊曰：「維應順元年歲次甲午，四月庚午朔。

translations.literal: At this time the Emperor received the investiture. The document said, "In the first year of Yingshun, year jiawu, on the first day of the fourth month, gengwu."
translations.idiomatic: At this point the emperor received the investiture document, which read: "In the first year of Yingshun, the jiawu year, on gengwu, the first day of the fourth month."

sentences.zh: 」帝回視房暠曰：「張濛神言甲庚午，不亦異乎！

translations.literal: " The Emperor turned to look at Fang Hao and said, "Zhang Meng's spirit-words said jiawu—how extraordinary!"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor turned to Fang Hao and said, "Zhang Meng's prophecy spoke of jiawu—is that not remarkable!"

sentences.zh: 」帝令暠共術士解三珠一珠事，言：「三珠，三帝也；

translations.literal: " The Emperor ordered Hao together with diviners to interpret the matter of three pearls and one pearl, saying, "Three pearls are three emperors;"
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered Hao and the diviners to interpret the three-pearls-become-one prophecy, saying, "The three pearls are three emperors;"

sentences.zh: 驢馬沒人驅，失位也。

translations.literal: "donkeys and horses driven by no man means loss of position."
translations.idiomatic: "donkeys and horses with no driver means loss of the throne."

sentences.zh: 」帝即位之後，以濛為將作少監同正，仍賜金紫以酬之。

translations.literal: After the Emperor ascended the throne, he made Meng vice director of imperial construction with full salary rank and bestowed gold and purple regalia as reward.
translations.idiomatic: After his accession he appointed Meng vice director of imperial construction with full salary and rewarded him with gold and purple regalia.

sentences.zh: 帝初封潞王，言事者云：「潞字一足已入洛矣。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was first enfeoffed as Prince of Lu, those who commented on affairs said, "In the character Lu, one foot has already entered Luo."
translations.idiomatic: When he was first enfeoffed as Prince of Lu, commentators said, "In the character for Lu, one foot has already entered Luo."

sentences.zh: 」又，帝在鳳翔日，有何叟者，年逾七十，暴卒，見陰官憑幾告叟曰：「為我言於潞王，來年三月當為天子，二十三年。

translations.literal: " Also, while the Emperor was at Fengxiang, there was an old man named He Sou, over seventy years old, who suddenly died. He saw an underworld official leaning on a desk who told Sou, "Speak to the Prince of Lu for me: next year in the third month he will become Son of Heaven for twenty-three years."
translations.idiomatic: " Also, while the prince was at Fengxiang, an old man named He Sou, over seventy, suddenly died. He saw an underworld official leaning on a desk who told him, "Tell the Prince of Lu for me: next year in the third month he will become emperor—for twenty-three years."

sentences.zh: 」叟既蘇，懼不敢言。

translations.literal: " When Sou revived, he was afraid and did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: " When Sou revived, he was too afraid to speak.

sentences.zh: 逾月復卒，陰官見而叱之曰：「安得違吾旨，不達其事，再放汝還。

translations.literal: After more than a month he died again. The underworld official saw him and rebuked him: "How dare you disobey my order and fail to convey the matter? I release you to return once more."
translations.idiomatic: More than a month later he died again. The underworld official rebuked him: "How dare you disobey my command and fail to deliver the message? I send you back once more."

sentences.zh: 」退見廊廡下簿書，以問主者，曰：「朝代將易，此即升降人爵之籍也。

translations.literal: " Retiring, he saw ledgers under the corridor and asked the keeper, who said, "The dynasty is about to change; this is the register by which human ranks rise and fall."
translations.idiomatic: " On his way out he saw ledgers under the corridor and asked the keeper, who said, "The dynasty is about to change; this is the register of promotions and demotions among the living."

sentences.zh: 」及蘇，詣帝親校劉延朗告之。

translations.literal: " When he revived, he went to the Emperor's personal attendant Liu Yanlang and told him.
translations.idiomatic: " When he revived, he went to the prince's personal attendant Liu Yanlang and told him.

sentences.zh: 帝召而問之，叟曰：「請質之，此言無征，戮之可也。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned and questioned him. Sou said, "Please verify it. If these words prove baseless, you may execute me."
translations.idiomatic: The prince summoned and questioned him. Sou said, "Put it to the test. If my words prove false, you may execute me."

sentences.zh: 」後人云：「二十三，蓋帝之小字也。

translations.literal: " Later people said, "Twenty-three was probably the Emperor's childhood name."
translations.idiomatic: " Later commentators said that "twenty-three" was probably the emperor's childhood name."

sentences.zh: 」又，石壕人胡杲通善天文，帝召問之，曰：「王貴不可言，若舉動，宜以乙未年。

translations.literal: " Also, Hu Gaotong of Shihao was skilled in astronomy. The Emperor summoned and questioned him. He said, "Your Highness's nobility is beyond words. If you take action, the year yiwei is appropriate."
translations.idiomatic: " Also, Hu Gaotong of Shihao was skilled in astronomy. The prince summoned him and asked. He said, "Your Highness's destiny is beyond words. If you act, the yiwei year is the right time."

sentences.zh: 」及舉兵，又問之，杲通曰：「今歲篰首，王者不宜建功立事，若俟來歲入朝，則福祚永遠矣。

translations.literal: " When he raised troops and asked again, Gaotong said, "This year is bishou; a king should not achieve merit and establish affairs. If you wait until next year to enter court, fortune and blessing will be far-reaching."
translations.idiomatic: " When he raised troops and asked again, Gaotong said, "This year is inauspicious for a king to win glory or establish his rule. If you wait until next year to enter the capital, your fortune will endure."

sentences.zh: 」其後皆驗。

translations.literal: " Afterward all were verified.
translations.idiomatic: " In time all of these proved true.

sentences.zh: 夫如是，則大寶之位，必有冥數，可輕道哉！

translations.literal: If it is so, then the position of great treasure must have a hidden mandate—how lightly can it be spoken of!
translations.idiomatic: If this is so, then the throne must be governed by a hidden mandate—how lightly can such things be discussed!

sentences.zh: 庚寅，鳳翔奏，西川孟知祥僭稱大蜀，年號明德。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Fengxiang reported that Meng Zhixiang of Xichuan had presumptuously styled himself Great Shu, with the era name Mingde.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Fengxiang reported that Meng Zhixiang of western Sichuan had presumptuously declared himself ruler of Great Shu, adopting the era name Mingde.

sentences.zh: 有司上言：「皇帝以五月朔日禦明堂殿受朝，三日夏至，祀皇地祇，前二日奏告獻祖室，不坐。

translations.literal: The relevant officials submitted a memorial: "The Emperor will on the first day of the fifth month ascend the Hall of Bright Hall to hold court and receive homage. On the third day is the summer solstice, when the Earth Spirit will be sacrificed to. Two days before, memorials will be presented at the Founding Ancestor's chamber, and he will not hold audience."
translations.idiomatic: The relevant officials memorialized: "Your Majesty will hold court at the Hall of Bright Hall on the first day of the fifth month. On the third day—the summer solstice—the emperor will sacrifice to the Earth Spirit. Two days prior, he will offer memorials at the Founding Ancestor's shrine and will not hold audience."

sentences.zh: 比正旦冬至，是日有祀事，則次日受朝。

translations.literal: Compared with New Year's Day and the winter solstice, when there are sacrificial affairs on that day, the court audience is held the following day.
translations.idiomatic: As with New Year's Day and the winter solstice, when sacrificial rites fall on the same day, the court audience should be held the following day.

sentences.zh: 今祀在五鼓前，質明行禮華，御殿在旦後，請比例行之。

translations.literal: Now the sacrifice is before the fifth watch; the rite is performed at dawn; ascending the hall is after daybreak. We ask that this be carried out by established precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The sacrifice is scheduled before the fifth watch, the rite to be performed at dawn, and the audience hall after sunrise. We request that precedent be followed.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「日出御殿，舉祀事無妨，宜依常年例。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "When the sun rises, ascend the hall; performing the sacrifice need not hinder this. Follow the usual annual precedent."
translations.idiomatic: " An edict replied: "Ascend the hall at sunrise; the sacrifice need not interfere. Follow the usual annual arrangement."

sentences.zh: 」史館奏：「凡書詔及處分公事，臣下奏議，望令近臣錄付當館。

translations.literal: " The Historiography Institute memorialized: "For all written edicts, disposition of public affairs, and ministers' memorials and deliberations, we request that close officials be ordered to copy and deliver them to this institute."
translations.idiomatic: " The Historiography Institute memorialized: "For all written edicts, official dispositions, and ministers' memorials, we ask that nearby officials be instructed to copy and deliver them to this institute."

sentences.zh: 」詔端明殿學士韓昭裔、樞密直學士李專美錄送。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered Han Zhaoyi, academician of the Hall of Enlightenment, and Li Zhuanmei, direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs, to copy and deliver them.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ordered Han Zhaoyi, academician of the Hall of Enlightenment, and Li Zhuanmei, direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs, to copy and forward the records.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以左諫議大夫盧損為右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Lu Sun, left remonstrance and counsel grandee, was appointed right attendant cavalry regular.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Lu Sun, left remonstrance and counsel grandee, was appointed right attendant cavalry regular.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，詔賜禁軍及鳳翔城下歸命將校錢帛各有差。

translations.literal: On renchen, an edict bestowed money and silks in varying amounts on the imperial guard and the officers who had surrendered below the walls of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, an edict bestowed money and silks in varying amounts on the imperial guard and the officers who had surrendered at Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》云：禁軍在鳳翔歸命者，自楊思權、尹暉等各賜二馬一駝、錢七十緡，下至軍人錢二十緡，其在京者各十緡。）〉

translations.literal: (The "Comprehensive Mirror" states: For the imperial guard who surrendered at Fengxiang, from Yang Siquan and Yin Hui onward each was granted two horses and one camel and seventy strings of cash; down to common soldiers, twenty strings; those in the capital, ten strings each.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Per the "Comprehensive Mirror": The imperial guards who had surrendered at Fengxiang—from Yang Siquan and Yin Hui on down—each received two horses, one camel, and seventy strings of cash; ordinary soldiers twenty strings; those in the capital ten strings each.)〉

sentences.zh: 初，帝離岐下，諸軍皆望以不次之賞，及從至京師，不滿所望，相與謠曰：「去卻生菩薩，扶起一條鐵。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor left below Qi, all the armies hoped for extraordinary rewards. When they followed him to the capital and their hopes were unmet, they circulated a ballad, saying, "We cast off the Living Bodhisattva and raised up a bar of iron."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the emperor left Fengxiang, every army expected extraordinary rewards. When they followed him to the capital and were disappointed, they circulated a ballad: "We cast off the Living Bodhisattva and raised up a bar of iron."

sentences.zh: 」其無厭如此。

translations.literal: " Such was their insatiable greed.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was their boundless discontent.

sentences.zh: 丙申，葬明宗皇帝於徽陵。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Emperor Mingzong was buried at Huiling.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Emperor Mingzong was buried at Huiling.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，奉神主於太廟。

translations.literal: On dingyou, his spirit tablet was installed in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, his spirit tablet was installed in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，山陵使、司空兼門下侍郎、平章事馮道上表納政，不允。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Feng Dao, commissioner for the imperial tomb, minister of works and vice director of the Secretariat, chief councilor, submitted a memorial resigning his office; it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Feng Dao, commissioner for the imperial tomb, minister of works and vice director of the Secretariat, and chief councilor, submitted a memorial to resign; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 五月庚子朔，禦文明殿受朝賀。

translations.literal: On gengzi, the first day of the fifth month, the Emperor ascended the Hall of Civilization to hold court and receive congratulatory homage.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, the first day of the fifth month, the emperor held court at the Hall of Civilization to receive congratulatory homage.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，以左龍武指揮使安審琦為左右捧聖都指揮使，以右千牛上將軍符彥饒為左右嚴衛都指揮使。

translations.literal: On yisi, An Shenqi, commander of the Left Dragon Martial Guard, was made commander-in-chief of the Left and Right Sacred Escort; Fu Yanrao, general of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard, was made commander-in-chief of the Left and Right Strict Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, An Shenqi, commander of the Left Dragon Martial Guard, was appointed commander-in-chief of the Left and Right Sacred Escort, and Fu Yanrao, general of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard, was appointed commander-in-chief of the Left and Right Strict Guard.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以端明殿學士韓昭允為樞密使；

translations.literal: On bingwu, Han Zhaoyun, academician of the Hall of Enlightenment, was appointed commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Han Zhaoyun, academician of the Hall of Enlightenment, was appointed commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs;

sentences.zh: 以莊宅使劉延朗為樞密副使；

translations.literal: Liu Yanlang, commissioner of the estate bureau, was made deputy commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanlang, commissioner of the estate bureau, was made deputy commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs;

sentences.zh: 以權知樞密事房暠為宣徽北院使；

translations.literal: Fang Hao, acting commissioner of military affairs, was appointed commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Attendant Service;
translations.idiomatic: Fang Hao, acting commissioner of military affairs, was appointed commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Attendant Service;

sentences.zh: 以成德軍節度使、大同彰國振武威塞等軍蕃漢馬步都部署、檢校太尉、兼中書令、駙馬都尉石敬瑭為北京留守、河東節度使，加檢校太師、兼中書令，都部署如故。

translations.literal: Shi Jingtang, military governor of the Chengde army, overall commander of the Han and non-Han cavalry and infantry of the Datong, Zhangguo, Zhenwu, Weisai, and other armies, honorary grand marshal, chief steward of the Secretariat, and imperial son-in-law, was made northern capital regent and military governor of Hedong, promoted to honorary grand preceptor and chief steward of the Secretariat, retaining his overall command as before.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jingtang, military governor of Chengde, overall commander of the Han and non-Han cavalry and infantry of Datong, Zhangguo, Zhenwu, Weisai, and other armies, honorary grand marshal, chief steward of the Secretariat, and imperial son-in-law, was made northern capital regent and military governor of Hedong, promoted to honorary grand preceptor and chief steward of the Secretariat, retaining his overall command.

sentences.zh: 汴州節度使、檢校太師、兼侍中、駙馬都尉趙延壽進封魯國公。

translations.literal: Zhao Yanshou, military governor of Bianzhou, honorary grand preceptor, chief steward, and imperial son-in-law, was advanced to Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshou, military governor of Bianzhou, honorary grand preceptor, chief steward, and imperial son-in-law, was advanced to Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 戊申，中書門下奏，太常禮院狀，明宗以此月二十日祔廟，宰臣攝太尉行事。

translations.literal: On wushen, the Secretariat memorialized that the Court of Imperial Sacrifices reported that Mingzong would be enshrined in the temple on the twentieth of this month, with the chief minister acting as grand marshal in the ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, the Secretariat reported that the Court of Imperial Sacrifices had stated Mingzong would be enshrined in the temple on the twentieth of this month, with the chief minister acting as grand marshal in the rite.

sentences.zh: 緣馮道在假，李愚十八日私忌，在致齋內，劉煦又奏判三司免祀事，

translations.literal: Because Feng Dao was on leave, Li Yu had a personal mourning day on the eighteenth and was within the fasting period, and Liu Xu memorialized to be exempted from sacrificial duties while managing the Three Departments,
translations.idiomatic: Because Feng Dao was on leave, Li Yu's personal mourning day fell on the eighteenth within the fasting period, and Liu Xu memorialized for exemption from sacrificial duties while managing the Three Departments,

sentences.zh: （《五代會要》：清泰元年五月，宰臣劉煦奏：「中書以近敕祠祭行事官致齋內，唯祀事得行，其餘悉斷。

translations.literal: (The "Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties": In the fifth month of the first year of Qingtai, chief minister Liu Xu memorialized: "The Secretariat, per a recent edict, holds that within the fasting period for sacrificial officiants, only sacrificial affairs may proceed; all else is suspended."
translations.idiomatic: (Per the "Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties": In the fifth month of the first year of Qingtai, chief minister Liu Xu memorialized: "The Secretariat, per a recent edict, holds that within the fasting period for sacrificial officiants, only sacrificial duties may proceed; all else is suspended."

sentences.zh: 又，宰臣行事致齋內，不押班，不赴內殿起居，不知印。

translations.literal: Also, chief ministers within the fasting period for sacrificial duties do not lead the court procession, do not attend inner-hall audiences, and do not affix seals.
translations.idiomatic: Also, chief ministers within the fasting period for sacrificial duties do not lead the court procession, do not attend inner-hall audiences, and do not affix seals.

sentences.zh: 臣緣判三司公事，其祀事、國忌、行香，伏乞特免。

translations.literal: As I am managing the affairs of the Three Departments, I humbly request special exemption from sacrificial duties, state mourning observances, and incense offerings."
translations.idiomatic: As I am managing the affairs of the Three Departments, I humbly request special exemption from sacrificial duties, state mourning observances, and incense offerings."

translations.literal: " Granted.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " Granted.)〉

sentences.zh: 詔禮官參酌。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the ritual officials to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the ritual officials to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 有司上言：「李愚私忌，在致齊內。

translations.literal: The relevant officials submitted a memorial: "Li Yu's personal mourning day falls within the fasting period."
translations.idiomatic: The relevant officials memorialized: "Li Yu's personal mourning day falls within the fasting period."

sentences.zh: 諸私忌日，遇大朝會入閣宣召，皆赴朝參。

translations.literal: On personal mourning days, when summoned for great court sessions or inner cabinet audiences, all attend court.
translations.idiomatic: On personal mourning days, when summoned for great court sessions or inner cabinet audiences, all attend court.

sentences.zh: 今祔廟事大，忌日屬私，請比大朝會宣召例。

translations.literal: The enshrinement is a great affair, yet the mourning day is private; we ask that the precedent for great court summons apply."
translations.idiomatic: The enshrinement is a great affair, yet the mourning day is private; we ask that the precedent for great court summons apply."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Granted.
translations.idiomatic: " Granted.

sentences.zh: 以陝府節度使康思立為邢州節度使，以同州節度使安重霸為西京留守，以羽林右第一軍都指揮使、春州刺史楊思權為邠州節度使。

translations.literal: Kang Sili, military governor of Shanfu, was made military governor of Xingzhou; An Chongba, military governor of Tongzhou, was made western capital regent; Yang Siquan, commander of the First Right Feathered Forest Army and prefect of Chunzhou, was made military governor of Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Sili, military governor of Shanfu, was appointed military governor of Xingzhou; An Chongba, military governor of Tongzhou, was made western capital regent; and Yang Siquan, commander of the First Right Feathered Forest Army and prefect of Chunzhou, was appointed military governor of Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 己酉，左監門衛將軍孔知鄴、右驍衛將軍華光裔並勒停見任。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Kong Zhiye, general of the Left Gate Guard, and Hua Guangyi, general of the Right Brave Guard, were both ordered to cease their current posts.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Kong Zhiye, general of the Left Gate Guard, and Hua Guangyi, general of the Right Brave Guard, were both ordered to cease their current posts.

sentences.zh: 時差知鄴應州告廟，稱疾辭命，改差光裔，復稱馬墜傷足，故俱罷之。

translations.literal: At the time Kong Zhiye had been dispatched to report at the temple in Yingzhou; he pleaded illness and declined the assignment. Guangyi was substituted, but then claimed a horse threw him and injured his foot—hence both were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Zhiye had been dispatched to report at the temple in Yingzhou but pleaded illness and declined; Guangyi was substituted but then claimed a fall from his horse had injured his foot—hence both were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以司空兼門下侍郎、平章事馮道為檢校太尉、同平章事，充同州節度使；

translations.literal: On gengxu, Feng Dao, minister of works and vice director of the Secretariat, chief councilor, was made honorary grand marshal and fellow chief councilor, and appointed military governor of Tongzhou;
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Feng Dao, minister of works and vice director of the Secretariat, and chief councilor, was made honorary grand marshal and fellow chief councilor, and appointed military governor of Tongzhou;

sentences.zh: 以天雄軍節度使範延光為樞密使，封齊國公；

translations.literal: Fan Yanguang, military governor of the Tianxiong army, was made commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and enfeoffed as Duke of Qi;
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang, military governor of Tianxiong, was appointed commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and enfeoffed as Duke of Qi;

sentences.zh: 鄆州節度使李從嚴為鳳翔節度使。

translations.literal: Li Congyan, military governor of Yanzhou, was made military governor of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Congyan, military governor of Yanzhou, was appointed military governor of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，以嚴衛都指揮使尹暉為齊州防禦使。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Yin Hui, commander-in-chief of the Strict Guard, was made defender of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Yin Hui, commander-in-chief of the Strict Guard, was appointed defender of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以侍衛馬軍都指揮、順化軍節度使安從進為河陽節度使，典軍如故。

translations.literal: On jiayin, An Congjin, cavalry commander of the imperial guard and military governor of Shunhua, was made military governor of Heyang, retaining command of the army as before.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, An Congjin, cavalry commander of the imperial guard and military governor of Shunhua, was appointed military governor of Heyang, retaining command of the army.

sentences.zh: 太常卿盧文紀奏：「明宗一室，酌獻舞曲，請名《雍熙之舞》。

translations.literal: Lu Wenji, grand master of ceremonies, memorialized: "For the chamber of Mingzong, the libation-presentation dance—please name it the "Dance of Universal Harmony.""
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wenji, grand master of ceremonies, memorialized: "For the chamber of Mingzong, the libation-presentation dance—please name it the "Dance of Universal Harmony.""

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Granted.
translations.idiomatic: " Granted.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以皇子銀青光祿大夫、檢校工部尚書重美為檢校司徒、守左衛上將軍。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Chongmei, the prince, silver-blue-light grand master for splendid happiness and honorary minister of works, was made honorary minister of education and acting general of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, the prince Chongmei, silver-blue-light grand master for splendid happiness and honorary minister of works, was made honorary minister of education and acting general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 自是，諸道節度使、刺史、文武臣僚，相繼加檢校官，或階爵封邑，以帝登位覃慶也。

translations.literal: From this time onward, military governors, prefects, and civil and military officials of every circuit successively received honorary appointments, or advances in rank, titles, and fiefs, in celebration of the Emperor's accession.
translations.idiomatic: From this point on, military governors, prefects, and civil and military officials across the circuits successively received honorary appointments or advances in rank, titles, and fiefs, in celebration of the emperor's accession.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以隴州防禦使相裏金為陝州節度使。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Xiangli Jin, defender of Longzhou, was made military governor of Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Xiangli Jin, defender of Longzhou, was appointed military governor of Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，帝以檄書告藩鄰，惟金遣判官薛文遇往來計事，故以節鎮獎之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor announced his accession to neighboring provinces by proclamation, Jin alone sent his aide Xue Wenyü back and forth to consult on affairs; therefore he was rewarded with a military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the emperor announced his accession to neighboring provinces by proclamation, Jin alone had sent his aide Xue Wenyü back and forth to consult on affairs; he was therefore rewarded with a military governorship.

sentences.zh: 宣徽北院使、檢校工部尚書房暠加檢校司空，行左威衛大將軍，使如故；

translations.literal: Fang Hao, commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Attendant Service and honorary minister of the Ministry of Works, was additionally made honorary grand minister of works, acting great general of the Left Majestic Guard, retaining his commission as before;
translations.idiomatic: Fang Hao, commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Attendant Service and honorary minister of the Ministry of Works, was additionally made honorary grand minister of works, acting great general of the Left Majestic Guard, retaining his commission;

sentences.zh: 以樞密使、左諫議大夫韓昭裔為刑部尚書，使如故。

translations.literal: Han Zhaoyi, commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and left remonstrance and counsel grandee, was made minister of justice, retaining his commission as before.
translations.idiomatic: Han Zhaoyi, commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and left remonstrance and counsel grandee, was appointed minister of justice, retaining his commission.

sentences.zh: 己未，太白晝見。

translations.literal: On jiwei, Venus was visible in daylight.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Venus was visible in daylight.

sentences.zh: 以樞密副使劉延朗為左領軍大將軍，職如故。

translations.literal: Liu Yanlang, deputy commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made great general of the Left Leading Army, retaining his duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yanlang, deputy commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was appointed great general of the Left Leading Army, retaining his duties.

sentences.zh: 庚申，左僕射、門下侍郎、平章事、監修國史李愚加特進，充太微宮使、宏文館大學士，餘如故。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Li Yu, left vice director, vice director of the Secretariat, chief councilor, and supervisor of the compilation of the national history, was granted special advancement, appointed commissioner of the Palace of Great Subtlety and grand academician of the Hall of Magnificent Literature, with the rest unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Li Yu, left vice director, vice director of the Secretariat, chief councilor, and supervisor of the national history, was granted special advancement and appointed commissioner of the Palace of Great Subtlety and grand academician of the Hall of Magnificent Literature, with other posts unchanged.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎、兼吏部尚書、同平章事、集賢院大學士、判三司劉煦加門下侍郎、兼吏部尚書、平章事、監修國史、判三司。

translations.literal: Liu Xu, vice director of the Secretariat, concurrent minister of personnel, fellow chief councilor, grand academician of the Academy of Assembled Worthies, and manager of the Three Departments, was additionally made vice director of the Secretariat, concurrent minister of personnel, chief councilor, supervisor of the compilation of the national history, and manager of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xu, vice director of the Secretariat, concurrent minister of personnel, fellow chief councilor, grand academician of the Academy of Assembled Worthies, and manager of the Three Departments, was additionally appointed vice director of the Secretariat, concurrent minister of personnel, chief councilor, supervisor of the national history, and manager of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，秦州奏，西川孟知祥出軍迫陷成州。

translations.literal: On guihai, Qinzhou reported that Meng Zhixiang of Xichuan had sent out an army and pressed forward to capture Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Qinzhou reported that Meng Zhixiang of western Sichuan had sent out an army and pressed forward to capture Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 以宣徽南院使、右驍衛大將軍郝瓊為左驍衛上將軍，職如故；

translations.literal: Hao Qiong, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Attendant Service and great general of the Right Brave Guard, was made general of the Left Brave Guard, retaining his duties as before;
translations.idiomatic: Hao Qiong, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Attendant Service and great general of the Right Brave Guard, was appointed general of the Left Brave Guard, retaining his duties;

sentences.zh: 以前義州刺史張承祐為武勝軍留後。

translations.literal: Zhang Chengyou, former prefect of Yizhou, was made acting military governor of Wusheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chengyou, former prefect of Yizhou, was appointed acting military governor of Wusheng.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以前右龍武統軍王景戡為右驍衛上將軍。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Wang Jingcan, former commander of the Right Dragon Martial Guard, was made general of the Right Brave Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Wang Jingcan, former commander of the Right Dragon Martial Guard, was appointed general of the Right Brave Guard.

sentences.zh: 六月庚午朔，改侍衛捧聖軍為彰聖，改嚴衛軍為寧衛。

translations.literal: On gengwu, the first day of the sixth month, the Imperial Guard Sacred Escort was renamed the Illustrious Sacred Guard, and the Strict Guard was renamed the Tranquil Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, the first day of the sixth month, the Imperial Guard Sacred Escort was renamed the Illustrious Sacred Guard, and the Strict Guard was renamed the Tranquil Guard.

sentences.zh: 壬申，封吳嶽成德公為靈應王，禮秩同五嶽。

translations.literal: On renshen, the Duke of Chengde of Mount Wu was enfeoffed as King of Spiritual Response, with ritual rank equal to the Five Sacred Peaks.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, the Duke of Chengde of Mount Wu was enfeoffed as King of Spiritual Response, with ritual rank equal to the Five Sacred Peaks.

sentences.zh: 帝初起，遣使祭嶽以求祐，及登祚，故有是報。

translations.literal: When the Emperor first rose in rebellion, he sent envoys to sacrifice at the sacred peak to seek divine aid; upon his accession, this reward followed.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first rose in rebellion, he had sent envoys to sacrifice at the sacred peak to seek divine aid; upon his accession, this reward followed.

sentences.zh: （《五代會要》載中書門下奏：天寶十載正月，封吳山成德公，與沂山、會稽、醫巫閭同封。

translations.literal: (The "Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties" records that the Secretariat memorialized: In the first month of the tenth year of Tianbao, the Duke of Chengde of Mount Wu was enfeoffed, together with Mount Yi, Mount Kuaiji, and Mount Yiwulü.)
translations.idiomatic: (Per the "Institutional Essentials of the Five Dynasties", the Secretariat memorialized: In the first month of the tenth year of Tianbao, the Duke of Chengde of Mount Wu was enfeoffed, together with Mount Yi, Mount Kuaiji, and Mount Yiwulü.)

sentences.zh: 至德二載十二月，改吳山為嶽，祠享官屬一同五嶽。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Zhide, Mount Wu was changed to a sacred peak, and its sacrificial officials and staff were made identical to those of the Five Sacred Peaks.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the second year of Zhide, Mount Wu was elevated to a sacred peak, and its sacrificial officials and staff were made identical to those of the Five Sacred Peaks.

sentences.zh: 今國家欲祈禱靈應，宜示殊禮，臣等商量，請加封為靈應王。
